uncertainty: P02 source JUNC-M is c. 1860, monochrome albumen (warm sepia), while P01/P03 sources are 2009-2013 colour. The c.1860 date is recorded as source_capture_time only; on screen P02 is a 'present' observation. Risk: a viewer could read the sepia junction as 'past'. Mitigation for U2: print it with the same warm stone grade as P01 (one global curve), keep it distinct from the cold memory print; if it still reads as 'old photo', switch to JUNC-F ground strip and record the switch (that re-catalogues P02 and blocks F2 until U3 confirms).

JUNC-M perspective is steep (street receding), not the 'frontal, slightly high' framing in plan §5; the multiplane glide should use the ground crop as the near plane and the far-fork crop as the far plane.
JUNC-M far crop contains a blurred carriage and a ghosted driver figure at distance; not a foreground figure, but U2 may mask it or keep the far plane out of focus.
DOOR-C, DOOR-S, BENCH dates are year-level from the LoC records (DOOR-S month-level); exact days are not given.
STOCK: LoC says the Federal Theatre Project collection is generally US government work but not analysed item by item.
The film's narrative route (P01->P02->P03) joins photographs from three cities; the ledger states this and no adjacency is claimed geographically.
Perec film dates (shot c.1976, broadcast 1978) not verified here; no material from it is used.

route.note: The route is a narrative order, not geography: the three source photographs are of Columbus OH, Paris and Sacramento CA. Nothing claims they are adjacent on a map.
